findings.summary: The Accounts security matrix is source-anchored but not semantically dispositive, so RED-FINAL-H1 is not genuinely closed.
findings.evidence: The fixture generator creates each of the six required security entries by copying the same whole-handler range and only changing an assertion label (generate-fixtures.py lines 188-207). The Red test then verifies only the entry-key set and that every entry repeats the route path and range digest (test lines 320-323); it never requires a disposition or a linked executable test/source assertion that establishes the stated authentication, authorization, validation, scope, audit, or destructive-effect result. For example, the public /api/health handler contains only a liveness response, yet its fixture has the same opaque reviewed-source-assertion shape for authentication, authorization, validation, audit, and destructive effect as an employee mutation. The contract therefore cannot distinguish an explicit documented not-applicable/public disposition from a fabricated or unsupported one.
findings.impact: A Green validator can accept all 17 routes with six mechanically duplicated anchors per route without proving the FR4 security dispositions or their executable/reviewed evidence. This preserves the semantic-vacuity problem identified by RED-FINAL-H1 despite correct path and range hashes.
findings.remediation: Before Green, make every security category carry a constrained explicit disposition and evidence kind (executable test reference or reviewed source assertion with category-specific rationale/anchor), and add positive/negative Red cases that reject an unsupported duplicated category, a missing disposition, and a public/global route labeled as an authenticated or tenant-scoped route without its documented exception.
